title: Phase 3.3: tag command — Create, list, delete, restore-from-tag
description:

- tag <AGENT> --list: List all tags for agent
- tag <AGENT> --delete <NAME>: Delete a tag

- Alphanumeric, underscore, hyphen, dot allowed (supports semver)
- Must not start with dash or dot
- Must be unique per agent

- Restore from tag: casb restore claude v1.0

JSON output formats:
- Create: {agent, name, tag, commit, success, dry_run}
- List: {agent, name, tags: [{tag, commit, date}]}
- Delete: {agent, name, tag, deleted, dry_run}

- Tag creation validates name format
- Tag creation validates commit reference
- Tag listing shows all tags with commit and date
- Tag deletion requires confirmation (skip with --force)

title: Phase 2.1: Git operations via std::process::Command
description:
Implement git operations using std::process::Command (NOT git2 crate).

Required git operations:
- git init --initial-branch=main (with fallback to git init)
- git add -A (stage all changes)
- git commit -m "message" (create commit)
- git log --format="..." (retrieve commit history)
- git tag (create, list, delete tags)
- git fsck --no-dangling (verify repo integrity)
- git diff --quiet HEAD (check for changes)
- git diff --cached --name-only (list staged files)
- git rev-parse --short HEAD (get short commit hash)
- git rev-parse --verify <ref> (validate commit/tag reference)
- git archive <commit> (extract backup for restore preview)
- git checkout <commit> -- . (restore specific commit)

Design:
- All git calls via std::process::Command
- Error handling with context (which git command failed)
- Dry-run support (skip actual git operations)
- Unit tests mocking git CLI responses

Success criteria:
- All git operations work correctly
- Error messages include command and output
- Dry-run mode skips git operations
- Works with git 2.30+

title: Phase 3.4: verify command — Backup integrity checks
description:

    "issues": 0,
    "warnings": 1,
    "details": ["Missing .gitignore file"]
  }
]

Success criteria:
- All integrity checks work correctly
- Issues vs warnings distinguished properly
- JSON output is valid array

- Summary shows verified/failed/skipped counts

title: Test: E2E integration tests with mock agent data
description:
Write E2E integration tests using mock agent data from generate_mock_agents.sh.

Test scenarios:
1. Full backup cycle:
   - casb init → creates backup location
   - casb backup → backs up all mock agents
   - casb list → shows all agents as backed_up
   - casb history claude → shows commit history
   - casb diff claude → shows no changes (just backed up)

2. Restore cycle:
   - Modify mock agent source
   - casb diff claude → shows changes
   - casb restore claude → restores from backup
   - Verify source matches backup

3. Tag workflow:
   - casb backup claude
   - casb tag claude v1.0
   - casb tag claude --list → shows v1.0
   - Modify source
   - casb backup claude
   - casb restore claude v1.0 → restores tagged version

4. Export/Import cycle:
   - casb export claude /tmp/test-export.tar.gz
   - Remove backup
   - casb import /tmp/test-export.tar.gz
   - Verify backup restored

5. Verify cycle:
   - casb verify → all pass
   - Corrupt a backup repo
   - casb verify → detects corruption

6. Doctor command:
   - casb doctor → all checks pass
   - Remove git temporarily
   - casb doctor → detects missing git

Test infrastructure:
- Use /tmp/casb-e2e-test-*/ as isolated test directory
- Use mock agent data from scripts/generate_mock_agents.sh
- Clean up after each test
- Detailed logging for debugging

title: Phase 4.3: hooks system — pre/post backup/restore hook execution
description:
Implement the hooks system for running scripts before/after backup and restore operations.

Hook directories (under ~/.config/casb/hooks/):
- pre-backup.d/: Run before any backup
- post-backup.d/: Run after successful backup
- pre-restore.d/: Run before any restore
- post-restore.d/: Run after successful restore

Hook execution rules:
- Scripts run in alphabetical order (e.g., 01-*.sh, 02-*.sh)
- Scripts must be executable
- Pre-hook failure aborts the operation
- Post-hook failure logs a warning but continues

Environment variables passed to hooks:
- CASB_AGENT: Agent name (e.g., 'claude')
- CASB_SOURCE: Source config path (e.g., '/home/user/.claude')
- CASB_BACKUP_DIR: Backup directory path
- CASB_OPERATION: 'backup' or 'restore'
- CASB_COMMIT: Commit hash (post-backup) or restore target

hooks command:
- hooks --list: List configured hooks

JSON output for hooks --list:
{
  "root": "/home/user/.config/casb/hooks",
  "hooks": {
    "pre-backup": ["01-notify.sh"],
    "post-backup": [],
    "pre-restore": [],
    "post-restore": []
  }
}

title: Custom agents with multiple locations lose data: all locations share one backup_subdir
description:
Code review HIGH. agent.rs:392-398 assigns every custom location backup_subdir '.{key}' — identical. sync_agent_to_backup syncs each location into same dir; sync_walkdir's prune_unknown deletes files from previous locations (kept only has current location's paths). Last location wins; earlier data silently absent from backup AND git commits the deletion. Restore mirror bug: same .key dir copied into every location.

FIX: distinct subdir per location (.{key}/loc0, loc1...) or reject multi-location custom agents. Regression test: 2-location custom agent, both trees survive backup+restore.

title: casb import unpacks attacker-controlled .git — hook/code-execution vector
description:
Code review HIGH security. export.rs:128-133 tar.unpack straight into backup_root; archives contain full .git. Imported archive can plant .git/hooks/* (exec bits preserved → next git commit/checkout/gc runs arbitrary code), .git/config core.hooksPath/fsmonitor/sshCommand/url.insteadOf, .gitmodules. tar 0.4.46 guards lexical .. but NOT symlink-then-write traversal.

FIX: unpack to temp, sanitize .git (strip hooks/, whitelist config keys), then move; or reject archives with .git/hooks; verify symlink traversal hardening. Add hostile-archive tests.
close_reason: fixed in commits 86e7903/612d2b0/dcd0bf3; verified adversarially under /tmp

title: export broken for qwencode + silently produces repo-only archives
description:
Code review HIGH. export.rs:69-102 assumes backup subdir == '.{key}'; qwencode uses '.qwen' → repo_path.join('.qwencode') missing → git checkout HEAD -- .qwencode fails SILENTLY (status discarded) → tar contains only .git. Same for ANY agent with no backup: 'successful' export leaks entire shared .git (all agents' history) with zero working files.

FIX: derive subdir via agent.backup_root_subdir() like history/stats; check checkout status, error NoBackupRepo when agent dir can't materialize; refuse export when commit_count_for_paths==0.

title: Agent credentials committed to plaintext git with no warning/exclusion

FIX: conservative default exclusions for credential filenames (opt-in re-include via .casbignore/config), AND/OR doctor/backup warning listing matched secret-looking files + README risk note. Decide per product intent; agent-first tool should not silently exfiltrate secrets into VCS.

title: Sync robustness batch: walkdir prune, file-location prune, perms, rsync stats, gitignore gaps
description:
Code review MED batch (sync.rs/backup.rs/restore.rs):
1. walkdir filter_entry doesn't prune excluded DIRS → traverses entire node_modules/projects/.venv trees when rsync unavailable. Skip descending when dir matches exclusion.
2. LocationKind::File never pruned when source file deleted → stale file stays tracked, restore resurrects deleted file. Remove dest + commit deletion.
3. walkdir/std::fs::copy drops file permissions (rsync -a preserves) → identical backups differ by backend; +x lost. set_permissions after copy.
4. rsync stats fiction: files_copied=all files in dest, bytes=dir_size, files_skipped always 0. Parse rsync --stats or count transferred only.
5. Agent-level + .casbignore exclusions never reach .gitignore → pre-exclusion files stay tracked forever; use git add pathspec excludes or document.
6. prune_stale_subdirs remove_dir_all's uninstalled agents' dirs → unstaged deletions forever, multi-machine hostile. Stage+commit prune or only remove untracked.
7. auto_commit=false still stages files → next commit attributes several agents' files to one message; HEAD-based cmds ignore staged work. Don't stage when auto_commit off, or warn.
8. restore compare_trees follows symlinks out of agent tree (read_dir/fs::read on symlinked dirs → scans ~/ etc). symlink_metadata + read_link compare, no descend.
9. compare_trees reads whole files into memory for every differing candidate → compare len first, hash/chunk.
close_reason: All 9 items fixed: dir pruning, file-loc prune, perms, rsync --stats, exclusion untrack (from secrets bead), prune staging+commit, auto_commit index hygiene, symlink-safe compare, chunked file compare. Plus worktree/export cleanup leaks and gitignore tracking. 6 new regression tests; 103+24 green.

- git gc --quiet every backup = full repack hourly → dominant cost; threshold it.
